newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia minister seeks domestic gas/power price cut.
newsitem.headline: Russia minister seeks domestic gas/power price cut.

text.p: Russia's fuel and energy ministry sent a draft resolution to the cabinet on Thursday to cut gas, power and railway tariffs with the aim of boosting tax revenue.

"We think that the rate of price rises for power and services of other natural monopolies, primarily railway transportation, does not correspond to the interests of national economic development," Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov told a news conference.
The draft plan provides for a 15 percent cut in gas prices, a 20 percent cut in electricity prices and up to 20 percent cuts in railway transportation charges, he said.
Rodionov said a fall in prices would make consumers more likely to pay and help untie the knot of non-payments crippling Russia's economy, and thus raise tax payments.
"It will not, of course, solve all problems, but this is the first necessary step to change the trend in the national economy," Rodionov said.

He said the economy and finance ministries fiercly opposed the draft plan, while the national gas monopoly RAO Gazprom, the national power grid RAO Unified Energy System and the Railway Ministry supported the plan.

The low level of tax revenue is one of the most serious problems facing the economy. The International Monetary Fund delayed payment of one tranche of its $10 billion loan earlier this year because of concern over revenues. The tranche was later released.
So far, the state coffers has received only 74 percent of targeted taxes, a government statement said.
Rodionov said that the oil and gas sector owes the government 10 trillion roubles in back taxes.
The government this week threatened six big companies with bankruptcy if they did not pay tax arrears within a week.
Last week President Boris Yeltsin set up an emergency commission, headed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, to improve tax collection.
